{{% callout type="info" %}}
**Where to find it:** Applications & Components → Comma → Model Edit → `uFit` (also on the Comma ribbon tab, Model Edit group)
{{% /callout %}}

Fits beam ends, plate edges, control lines and rebar ends to a picked reference: a face, a plane, or a line. Set the reference and gap, pick the reference, then pick the objects to fit.

**How to use:**

1.  Choose *Reference* (Face, Plane 3 points (pick exactly three points), Line, or Line 2 points.) and a *Gap*, or preselect the objects before you click Apply.
2.  Click **Apply**, pick the reference, then pick the objects to fit if none were preselected. Finish a multiple pick with the middle mouse button.
3.  The command repeats until you press <kbd>Esc</kbd>.

| Option | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| **Reference** | Face, Plane 3 points (pick exactly three points), Line, or Line 2 points. |
| **Gap** | Signed, in mm. Shifts the plane along its normal (reversing the point order of a 3-point plane reverses the normal). The Gap list remembers the last five applied values while Tekla runs. |
| **Beam OBB** | For beams, uses the part's oriented bounding box to choose the projected candidate instead of the raw handle. |

Supports beam endpoints and height, PANEL PolyBeam height, ordinary PolyBeam endpoints (not with a Line reference), ControlLine endpoints, bolt group positions, ContourPlate edges and BentPlate legs. ContourPlate and BentPlate fitting keep the surviving contour points and chamfers; picked-edge options for plates are in **uFitPlate**.

Rebar: SingleRebar and polygonal RebarGroup, with a Face or Plane reference only. The end whose input point is nearer the plane moves along its end leg onto the plane (Gap shifts the plane). Only input points move: hooks, end offsets and bend radii stay as they are, so the physical bar end stays short of the plane by the bar's end offset (a 4 mm end offset ends 4 mm before the plane); use Gap to compensate. Bars owned by a component, bars generated by a RebarSet, bars with child objects, and spiral or curved groups are skipped and listed. A one-polygon group is also skipped when its bar ends are not parallel to the plane, because only the defining bar would reach it.

Rebar sets: pick the set or any bar it generated and uFit edits the set, never the generated bars. The leg face edge the bars end on moves onto the plane (Gap shifts the plane), the set regenerates and every bar follows; a slanted plane puts each bar end on the slanted line. Hooks, spacing and the other edges stay as they are. At the fitted edge the bars end exactly on the plane: a set made from its host drops its end inset there (tested: 32 mm became 0), so use Gap if you want cover. If a set keeps an end inset at that edge, the fit is undone and the report names the inset. A set is skipped and listed when its bars end on more than one leg face edge or leg face, when a bar ends outside its leg face, when the plane is parallel to the leg face, when the fit would fold a bar, and when a component owns the set. The result is read back after the change and the leg face is restored if a bar does not end where the geometry predicts. This edits the leg face of the set, so check it against the host.

{{% callout type="warning" %}}
For a beam parallel to the reference plane the height branch changes the profile to a rectangle (height × width), which can replace an I, U, L or M profile. Check profiles after fitting such beams.
{{% /callout %}}

**More details:**

-   Fit modifies Beam endpoints/height, PANEL PolyBeam height/contour translation, ControlLine endpoints and the input points at the ends of SingleRebar and polygonal RebarGroup.
-   Face, Plane through three points, native Line and Line through two points are available.
-   Pick a reference, then targets, or preselect targets before launching.
-   Beam Line fitting converts Gap by the angle to the stored endpoint axis.
-   Beam OBB uses section bounds to choose a projected candidate; ControlLine ignores that option.
-   Plane/ControlLine ties edit Start/Point1; Beam Line ties edit End.
-   ContourPlate supports all four reference modes with gap, default seed selection, sequential individual-edge fitting and two post-fit cleanup passes.
-   Surviving contour point identities/chamfers are retained.
-   BentPlate Face/Plane uses automatic free-edge group selection; Line/Line2Points selects a current free edge independently for each manual leg.
-   Both use sequential leg fitting, with checked whole-geometry Modify/restoration.
-   BentPlate uses the fixed MPD Fit mean-distance strategy and minimize behavior.
-   Advanced picked-edge options belong to Fit Plate.
-   For a Beam parallel to the reference plane, the height branch changes the profile to height\*width and may translate both endpoints.
-   This can convert the profile shape to a rectangle, including I/U/L/M profiles.
-   Apply saves attributes and starts a new command; The Gap list keeps the last five applied values.
-   PolyBeam Type PANEL supports Face/Plane height fitting: rectangular profile and conditional translation of every contour point.
-   Ordinary PolyBeam types support Face/Plane endpoint fitting; all PolyBeam Line modes are unsupported by the MPD Edit 2.00.2 reference command and are reported without changes.
-   Ordinary PolyBeam fitting uses raw first/last contour segments, ignoring OBB and retaining chamfers.
-   Two nearly parallel segments (0.08 radians) are skipped.
-   Collapsed segments are rejected.
-   BoltGroup Plane fitting offsets the plane once and edits the nearest First/SecondPosition (tie First).
-   Line fitting uses the closest point on the bolt axis and direct axial Gap (tie Second), without Beam angle conversion.
-   OBB is ignored.
-   Check the pattern, attached parts and holes after fitting.
-   Selected BooleanPart resolves its current operative Part.
-   Operative Beam uses the Beam adapters; operative ContourPlate supports all four references through the same checked writer; operative BentPlate uses the same four reference modes and checked writer.
-   The BooleanPart and operative share an ID; edits retain Father and operation type.
-   Plate Line builds a target plane through the reference line using the plate normal.
-   Gap shifts that plane along LineDirection cross PlateNormal; reversing the line reverses the positive Gap side.
-   Beam angle conversion and OBB do not apply to plate Line.
-   A line parallel to the plate normal cannot define the target plane and is reported before mutation.
-   Rebar supports Face and Plane references only (Line references are reported without changes).
-   The end whose input point is nearer the plane moves along its end leg onto the plane, with Gap shifting the plane; ties edit the first point.
-   Gap supports metric arithmetic or imperial feet/inch fractions according to XS\_IMPERIAL\_INPUT at dialog opening.
-   Blank retains the prior gap.
-   Invalid input blocks Apply; history displays matching units.
-   Reopen after unit changes.
-   On opening, standard attributes load and normalize: absolute Gap above 1e9 mm becomes 0, negative Mode selects the first reference, UseObb normalizes to No/Yes.
-   Normalized attributes apply without starting a model operation.
